messages:
sophie: FYI a customer hit a weird one — they tried to create a new API key via the Console and the request to POST /v1/keys returned a 403 that the UI then shows as "invalid api key". They can still list keys but cannot create new ones. Customer says billing looks fine.
harry: can you paste the raw response body/logs?
sophie: pasted below from their repro session:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/keys -H 'Authorization: Bearer <user_token>' -d '{"name":"new-key"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "message": "Authentication failed"
}
x-tenant-id: org_98765
x-feature-flags: membership_api_keys=false
```
They also included a screenshot from Console saying "Invalid API key" when clicking Create.

michael: :thinking_face: that error looks like it's coming from auth middleware but the x-feature-flags header is interesting — `membership_api_keys=false` means the feature gate disallowed key creation. We intentionally short-circuited in the entitlement filter and returned 403 but used the generic auth error code.

tara: this is the class of problem where plan/membership gating is masquerading as auth. We had a backlog item to return clearer errors for plan blocks. Ticketing it now. support-bot: Created INC-2050: membership-tier blocks API key creation (assigned: michael).

harry: can we confirm root cause in code? michael: checked the entitlement-checker handler in service-auth. In the path `POST /v1/keys` we call `check_feature(member_id, "api_key_create")`. If false we throw an AuthError(code="invalid_api_key", status=403). Should be throwing EntitlementError(code="membership_plan_block", status=403) with a distinct error_code and message. Right now SDKs map `invalid_api_key` -> prompt user to rotate key which confuses customers.

sophie: customer report: they downgraded an org license last week and then tried to add a second key. Seems the seat/feature wasn't carried over but billing portal shows active sub. Could be a sync lag between billing and license service.

michael: repro steps I used locally:
```
# set org to trial_expired
POST /internal/admin/orgs/org_98765/flags {"membership_api_keys": false}
# attempt create
curl -X POST /v1/keys -H 'Authorization: Bearer <user_token>' -d '{"name":"x"}'
# response shows 403 invalid_api_key
```
Fix plan: 1) change entitlement-checker to return `error.code = "membership_plan_block"` and include `error.hint = "billing: membership tier blocks key creation; see billing console"` (michael) 2) update SDK error mapping to surface plan-blocks separately and not suggest rotating keys (tara) 3) add a short-term support workaround to toggle the feature flag or issue a manual override (sophie).

tara: low-risk patch prepared. I'll open PR to change error codes and add a mapping in the SDK to show actionable message. Also will add an observability metric `entitlement_block.reason=membership_plan` so we can filter logs.

sophie: temporary workaround shared with customer: ask them to open Billing -> Subscriptions -> Manage -> Re-sync license (if button available) or we can trigger `POST /internal/admin/orgs/org_98765/resync_billing` for them. Also offered manual override to let them create one key while we push fix. Customer accepted manual override.

harry: should we change server status code to 402 Payment Required? maybe confusing. tara: prefer keep 403 but change error code and message; 402 has other implications/api clients might not expect.

michael: PR link: https://git.redwood/infer/entitlement/merge_requests/321 — it updates the error payload, adds metric, and unit tests. Will follow up with SDK team to cut a patch.

sophie: thanks everyone — created follow-up customer note and flagged for billing sync run. Closing thread after deploy and confirmation. :white_check_mark:
